newsitem.title: GERMANY: EMI says discussing small bank access to ECB.
newsitem.headline: EMI says discussing small bank access to ECB.

text.p: European Monetary Institute President Alexandre Lamfalussy said on Wednesday the EMI council was discussing how to enable small or specialised institutions to have direct access to credit from the future European central bank.
At the moment, banks in a number of European Union countries can obtain funds to finance their business directly from their respective central banks.

"In my opinion, a direct and uncomplicated means of obtaining central bank money should also continue to be available to these banks after the start" of currency union, Lamfalussy said in the text of the speech to a banking group.

"I feel it would be inadvisable if the introduction of the single monetary policy meant turning the existing refinancing habits and practices in the various countries completely upside down," he said in the speech in Duesseldorf.
"I am confident that the EMI council will find a compromise solution," he said.

As an example of the current system, he said smaller banks in Germany have direct access to primary liquidity from the Bundesbank, within the limits of their individual rediscount quotas through the discount credit facility even if they do not participate in regular tenders for central bank money.

Lamfalussy said that he could envisage that the future European central bank, in addition to its normal weekly tender operations, might also offer open market operations at longer maturities, which would accommodate needs of smaller banks.
